There is a positive, fully explicit triangle witness.  Let \(n=3\), let
\[
G=\begin{bmatrix}0&1&1\\1&0&1\\1&1&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\nu(w)=\left(\frac13\right)^{\sum_iw_i}
       \left(\frac23\right)^{3-\sum_iw_i},
\]
and, writing \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\), define
\[
f_i(w)=
\begin{cases}
1,&w_i=1\text{ and }w_j=w_k=0,\\
0,&w_i=0\text{ and }w_j+w_k\ge1,\\
\star,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Take \(F_1=F_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(\kappa=1/8\).  With \(J_3=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}\) and \(A=(I_3+J_3)/4\), the exact design and endpoint inputs are
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
\[
c_L=-\frac14,
\qquad c_U=\frac14,
\qquad
Q(c_L)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix}.
\]
For normalized representatives \(B(x,y)=\begin{bmatrix}x&0\\0&y\end{bmatrix}\), the full optimizer correspondences are
\[
\mathcal A_0=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=\mathbf 1^{\top}y=x^{\top}y=0
\right\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=x^{\top}y=0,\ 
(\mathbf 1^{\top}y)^2=\frac{216}{55}
\right\}.
\]
They are nonempty, and their exact objective values satisfy
\[
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\qquad
w(B_0)=\frac{521}{1200}\quad(B_0\in\mathcal A_0),
\qquad
w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{2613}{8432}
\quad(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}).
\]
Moreover every member of \(\mathcal A_0\cup\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) obeys
\[
\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=\frac4{27}.
\]
Consequently \(\xi_0=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak X_\kappa\), and the rational choices
\[
\delta=\frac{4912}{39525},
\qquad
\eta=\frac5{216}
\]
give the full-correspondence certificates
\[
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_0)
-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=\delta>0
\]
and
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}
\left\{\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\right\}
=\eta>0.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Write \(\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1_3\).  We first enumerate the support of the known assignment law.  The all-zero and all-one assignments expose no unit to either displayed label.  If only unit \(i\) is treated, then \(D_{i,1}=1\) and \(D_{j,0}=1\) for each \(j\ne i\).  If exactly units \(i,j\) are treated, then \(D_{k,0}=1\) for the remaining unit \(k\).  The exposure events are therefore mutually exclusive within each unit, as required by ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures, and
\[
 \pi_{i,1}=\frac{4}{27},
 \qquad
 \pi_{i,0}=2\frac{4}{27}+\frac{2}{27}=\frac{10}{27}>0.
 \tag{1}
\]
Thus every division by an exposure probability below is supported.  Direct intersection probabilities give, for \(i\ne j\),
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 &i=j&i\ne j\\ \hline
 \operatorname{Cov}_{\nu}(D_{i,1},D_{j,1})&92/729&-16/729\\
 \operatorname{Cov}_{\nu}(D_{i,1},D_{j,0})&-40/729&68/729\\
 \operatorname{Cov}_{\nu}(D_{i,0},D_{j,0})&170/729&8/729.
\end{array}
\tag{2}
\]
For example, the off-diagonal event \(D_{i,1}D_{j,0}=1\) is the singleton assignment treating \(i\), and hence has probability \(4/27=108/729\); subtracting \((4/27)(10/27)=40/729\) gives \(68/729\).  Similarly, \(D_{i,0}D_{j,0}=1\) is the singleton assignment treating the third unit and has probability \(4/27\).  Equations (1)--(2) prove the asserted formulas for \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\).  Ass:known-exposure makes the two displayed labels legitimate potential-outcome exposures; outcomes under the label \(\star\) do not enter the calculations.

For a Bernoulli \((1/2)\) variable, \(\mu_a=1/2\), \(\sigma_a^2=1/4\), and its quantile takes only the values zero and one.  The countermonotone and comonotone quantile integrals defining the two covariance endpoints consequently give
\[
 c_L=0-\frac14=-\frac14,
 \qquad
 c_U=\frac12-\frac14=\frac14.
 \tag{3}
\]
Substitution in def:moment-matrix gives the displayed endpoint matrices: each diagonal block is
\[
 \frac14J_3+\frac14I_3=A,
\]
whereas the cross block \(-J_3/4-cI_3\) is \((I_3-J_3)/4\) at \(c_L\) and \(-A\) at \(c_U\).

We next certify the global optimizer equality sets.  Fix a normalized representative \(B(x,y)\in\mathcal B_{1/8}\), and put
\[
 s=\mathbf 1^{\top}x,
 \qquad
 t=\mathbf 1^{\top}y,
 \qquad
 q=x^{\top}y.
\]
The normalization in def:kappa-basis-class and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality imply
\[
 0\le s^2\le9,
 \qquad
 0\le t^2\le9.
 \tag{4}
\]
Block multiplication using the verified \(\Omega\) gives
\[
 S_B=
 \begin{bmatrix}
 \dfrac49-\dfrac{16s^2}{729}&-\dfrac{4q}{27}+\dfrac{68st}{729}\\[4pt]
 -\dfrac{4q}{27}+\dfrac{68st}{729}&\dfrac23+\dfrac{8t^2}{729}
 \end{bmatrix}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Define
\[
 d=729+12t^2-36s^2-54q^2+68qst-22s^2t^2.
 \tag{6}
\]
Equation (5) yields
\[
 \det(S_B)=\frac{8d}{19683}.
 \tag{7}
\]
The rank boundary is explicit: membership in \(\mathcal B_{1/8}\) implies \(S_B\succeq(3/8)I_2\).  Therefore \(d>0\), every ordinary inverse used below exists, and no division is made at a singular basis or at the \(\kappa\)-boundary.

For a checkable reduction of the objective algebra, let \(C_B=\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\).  Its two block rows are
\[
 C_B=
 \begin{bmatrix}
 x-\dfrac{4s}{27}\mathbf1&-y+\dfrac{17t}{27}\mathbf1\\[3pt]
 -\dfrac25x+\dfrac{34s}{135}\mathbf1&\dfrac35y+\dfrac{4t}{135}\mathbf1
 \end{bmatrix}.
 \tag{8}
\]
Writing \(Q_L=Q(c_L)\) and \(Q_U=Q(c_U)\), equations (4)--(8) give
\[
 C_B^{\top}Q_LC_B=
 \begin{bmatrix}
 (1195s^2+6561)/24300&-(729q-1820st)/12150\\
 -(729q-1820st)/12150&(1240t^2+729)/6075
 \end{bmatrix},
 \tag{9}
\]
and
\[
 C_B^{\top}Q_UC_B=
 \begin{bmatrix}
 3(49-5s^2)/100&(5st-14q)/25\\
 (5st-14q)/25&(48-5t^2)/25
 \end{bmatrix}.
 \tag{10}
\]
The trace identities in def:gain-loss now yield
\[
 \begin{split}
 g_B(c_L)
 &=\frac{76545+9891s^2+30732t^2-5832q^2+18232qst-10460s^2t^2}{1200d},\\
 g_B(c_U)
 &=\frac{3\{66825-5181s^2-2652t^2-6048q^2+5968qst-1260s^2t^2\}}{400d}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{11}
\]
The uncontrolled endpoint traces are
\[
 h(c_L)=\frac{313}{600},
 \qquad
 h(c_U)=\frac{171}{200}.
 \tag{12}
\]

Because def:moment-matrix is affine in \(c\) and zero is the midpoint of \([c_L,c_U]\), def:gain-loss gives
\[
 g_B(0)=\frac{g_B(c_L)+g_B(c_U)}2.
\]
Combining this identity with (11),
\[
 \frac{31}{80}-g_B(0)=\frac{N_0(s,t,q)}{1200d},
 \tag{13}
\]
where
\[
 N_0=5022q^2-4352qst+670s^2t^2+1629s^2+2148t^2.
\]
Completing the square gives
\[
 N_0
 =5022\left(q-\frac{1088}{2511}st\right)^2
 +1629s^2+2148t^2-\frac{685118}{2511}s^2t^2.
 \tag{14}
\]
The last three terms are a bilinear function of \((u,v)=(s^2,t^2)\in[0,9]^2\).  Its values at the four vertices are, respectively,
\[
 0,
 \qquad14661,
 \qquad19332,
 \qquad\frac{368665}{31}.
 \tag{15}
\]
A bilinear function on this rectangle is the convex combination of its four vertex values with the usual bilinear interpolation weights.  Hence (14) is nonnegative.  Moreover, equality in its bilinear part forces \(s=t=0\), and equality in the square then forces \(q=0\).  Since \(d>0\), (13) proves
\[
 \max_{B\in\mathcal B_{1/8}}g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80}
\]
with equality exactly when \(s=t=q=0\), provided such bases are feasible.  They are: for these invariants, (5) becomes \(\operatorname{diag}(4/9,2/3)\), so
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=\frac4{27}>\frac18.
 \tag{16}
\]
The equality set is nonempty; for example, one may take
\[
 x=\sqrt{\frac32}(1,-1,0)^{\top},
 \qquad
 y=\frac1{\sqrt2}(1,1,-2)^{\top}.
\]
This proves the asserted full description of \(\mathcal A_0\).  Substitution in (11)--(12) gives
\[
 g_B(c_L)=\frac7{80},
 \qquad
 g_B(c_U)=\frac{11}{16},
\]
and hence
\[
 w(B)=\max\left\{\frac{313}{600}-\frac7{80},
 \frac{171}{200}-\frac{11}{16}\right\}
 =\frac{521}{1200}
 \qquad(B\in\mathcal A_0).
 \tag{17}
\]

We now give a matching global lower-bound certificate for the primary minimax problem.  Let
\[
 \lambda=\frac{1407}{2635}\in(0,1),
 \qquad
 v=\frac{2613}{8432},
\]
and abbreviate \(\ell_L=\ell_B(c_L)\) and \(\ell_U=\ell_B(c_U)\).  Since a maximum dominates every convex combination, (11)--(12) give
\[
 \begin{split}
 w(B)-v
 &\ge \lambda\ell_L+(1-\lambda)\ell_U-v\\
 &=\frac{3N_{\mathrm{mm}}(s,t,q)}{210800d},
 \end{split}
 \tag{18}
\]
where
\[
 N_{\mathrm{mm}}
 =274734q^2-281644qst+68986s^2t^2+34527s^2.
\]
Another exact square completion yields
\[
 N_{\mathrm{mm}}
 =274734\left(q-\frac{70411}{137367}st\right)^2
 +s^2\left(34527-\frac{439017980}{137367}t^2\right).
 \tag{19}
\]
By (4), the coefficient in the second term is bounded below by
\[
 34527-9\frac{439017980}{137367}
 =\frac{87967621}{15263}>0.
 \tag{20}
\]
Thus (18) proves \(w(B)\ge v\) over the entire feasible class, and equality in the second line of (18) occurs exactly when \(s=q=0\).  Because both weights in the first line of (18) are positive, equality \(w(B)=v\) additionally requires \(\ell_L=\ell_U\).  When \(s=q=0\), direct simplification of (11)--(12) gives
\[
 \ell_L-\ell_U
 =-\frac{3(55t^2-216)}{10(4t^2+243)}.
 \tag{21}
\]
The denominator in (21) is positive on the support (4).  Consequently equality in the minimax lower bound holds exactly when
\[
 s=0,
 \qquad q=0,
 \qquad t^2=\frac{216}{55}.
 \tag{22}
\]
Conversely, (18)--(21) show that every basis satisfying (22) has both endpoint losses equal to \(v\).  Such bases exist.  Indeed, choose a normalized \(y\) with \((\mathbf1^{\top}y)^2=216/55<9\); because the inequality is strict, \(y\) is not parallel to \(\mathbf1\).  Then choose normalized \(x\) in the one-dimensional orthogonal complement of \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1,y\}\).  For every such pair, (5) is diagonal with entries
\[
 \frac49,
 \qquad
 \frac23+\frac{8t^2}{729},
\]
so the basis is feasible and again satisfies (16).  This proves both the claimed full description of \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and
\[
 v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{2613}{8432}.
 \tag{23}
\]

Finally, the positive exposure probabilities in (1), the Bernoulli marginals on \([0,1]\), and the feasible bases constructed above verify the defining predicates of def:lawful-instance-class.  Hence \(\xi_0\in\mathfrak X_{1/8}\).  Equations (16), (17), and (22)--(23) apply to every member of the two optimizer correspondences, not merely to selected representatives.  Therefore
\[
 \Delta(\xi_0)
 =\frac{521}{1200}-\frac{2613}{8432}
 =\frac{4912}{39525}=\delta>0,
 \tag{24}
\]
and the optimizer-wide regularity slack is
\[
 \frac4{27}-\frac18=\frac5{216}=\eta>0.
 \tag{25}
\]
Thus the certificate compares the full nondegenerate equality set of the minimax-residual rule with the full equality set of the Zhao-type zero-covariance surrogate \(\mathcal A_0\); it is not merely a comparison of two selected bases.  Equations (24)--(25) are precisely the asserted strict-separation and interior-regularity certificates. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For every moment-complete input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying exposure positivity and \(\kappa\)-feasibility, and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), the candidate projective interval branch-and-bound procedure terminates after finitely many subdivisions and returns a checkable certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) such that
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad
U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\varepsilon}.
\]
Here \(B_{\varepsilon}\in\mathcal B_\kappa\) is represented exactly, including when the feasible set has no relative interior and lies on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  A chart box meeting that equality boundary is never discarded as infeasible; it may be discarded only when its certified objective lower bound exceeds the incumbent upper bound.  Consequently, along any sequence \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and retained-box mesh diameters converge to zero.  This is a finite, instance-dependent termination result; it asserts neither a uniform complexity bound nor a semidefinite-program reduction.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let
\[
K_\kappa=\left\{(b_1,b_0):
\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n,\quad
\lambda_{\min}\!\left(n^{-1}B(b_1,b_0)^{\top}\Omega
B(b_1,b_0)\right)\geq\kappa\right\}.
\]
The assumption of \(\kappa\)-feasibility makes \(K_\kappa\) nonempty.  By the compactness argument in Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}kappa\mbox{-}exhaustion}\), it is a closed subset of the product of two radius-\(\sqrt n\) spheres, and its image after the independent projective sign identifications is the compact set \(\mathcal B_\kappa\).  Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined.  Moreover, for every \(B\in K_\kappa\),
\[
S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\succeq n\kappa I_2,
\qquad
\lVert S_B^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq (n\kappa)^{-1}. \tag{1}
\]

For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), put \(Q_e=Q(c_e)\) and write the endpoint loss as
\[
\ell_e(B)
=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left(\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q_e\right)
-n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q_e\Pi^{-1}\Omega B
\right]. \tag{2}
\]
Equation (1) and the continuity of matrix multiplication, inversion on the positive-definite cone, and trace show that both functions \(\ell_L\) and \(\ell_U\) are continuous on \(K_\kappa\).  Consequently
\[
w(B)=\max\{\ell_L(B),\ell_U(B)\} \tag{3}
\]
is continuous.  The expressions in (2) are unchanged by independently changing the signs of the two normalized columns, so (3) descends to a continuous function on \(\mathcal B_\kappa\).  Compactness therefore gives an attained minimum \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and a nonempty compact minimizer set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\).

We next establish the finite and effective part of the claim.  The finitely many signed pivot charts in the stated procedure cover both normalized projective factors: on a vector of squared norm \(n\), at least one coordinate has absolute value at least \(1\), and hence at least \(n^{-1/2}\).  On each closed chart box, the moment-complete input gives outward-rounded enclosures of every coefficient in (2), effective refinement moduli, and an exact decision whether the box meets the sphere constraints and the inequality defining \(K_\kappa\), including equality in that inequality.  Because \(\kappa>0\), continuity of \(S_B\), compactness, and (1) imply that sufficiently small boxes meeting \(K_\kappa\) admit a certified neighborhood bound
\[
S_B\succeq \frac{n\kappa}{2}I_2 \tag{4}
\]
throughout the box.  Thus ordinary interval evaluation of the two-by-two inverse is valid on every such box.  The effective refinement moduli, together with (4), imply the following effective uniform statement: for every positive rational \(\alpha\), after finitely many bisections and finitely much coefficient-oracle refinement, each chart box \(C\) that meets \(K_\kappa\) has outward-rounded rational intervals
\[
I_e(C)=[\underline\ell_{e,C},\overline\ell_{e,C}],
\qquad
\{\ell_e(B):B\in C\cap K_\kappa\}\subseteq I_e(C),
\qquad
\operatorname{wid}\{I_e(C)\}\leq\alpha,
\tag{5}
\]
for \(e\in\{L,U\}\).  This is not an appeal to an uneffective compactness principle: for exact rational or real-algebraic input the requisite arithmetic bounds are computed exactly, while for inclusion-oracle input the required stopping depths are supplied by the effective refinement moduli in \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\).  The positive lower bounds needed for division are eventually certified because exposure positivity and \(\kappa>0\) separate the finitely many relevant denominators from zero.

Taking componentwise maxima in (5) gives
\[
I_w(C)=[\underline w_C,\overline w_C]
=\left[
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\underline\ell_{e,C},
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\overline\ell_{e,C}
\right],
\quad
\{w(B):B\in C\cap K_\kappa\}\subseteq I_w(C),
\quad
\overline w_C-\underline w_C\leq\alpha. \tag{6}
\]
The last inequality follows from
\(\max_e\overline\ell_{e,C}\leq
\max_e(\underline\ell_{e,C}+\alpha)
=\max_e\underline\ell_{e,C}+\alpha\).

There is also an exact feasible point name for every box \(C\) declared feasible.  Starting from \(C\), bisect and use the exact feasibility decision to select, in a fixed order, a child that still meets \(K_\kappa\).  This produces nested nonempty compact sets \(C_j\cap K_\kappa\) whose diameters tend to zero.  Their intersection is a singleton \(\{B_C\}\) with \(B_C\in K_\kappa\).  The finite rule that returns the successive boxes on request is a certified inclusion-oracle name for \(B_C\), exactly of the kind authorized in \(\mathscr K_\varepsilon\).  This argument does not require relative interior and applies unchanged when every feasible point satisfies
\[
\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)=\kappa. \tag{7}
\]

Fix the exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), and effectively choose a positive rational \(\alpha\) such that \(4\alpha<\varepsilon\).  Refine the finite chart cover until (5) holds and every surviving box has chart diameter at most \(\varepsilon\).  Exact feasibility deletes precisely the boxes disjoint from \(K_\kappa\).  Let \(\mathcal P\) be the resulting finite family of nonempty boxes and construct \(B_C\) for every \(C\in\mathcal P\).  Choose
\[
C_0\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{C\in\mathcal P}\overline w_C,
\qquad
B_\varepsilon=B_{C_0},
\qquad
U_\varepsilon=\overline w_{C_0},
\qquad
L_\varepsilon=\min_{C\in\mathcal P}\underline w_C. \tag{8}
\]
All comparisons and both bounds in (8) are rational and checkable.  If \(B^\star\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(C^\star\in\mathcal P\) contains a representative of \(B^\star\), validity of (6) gives
\[
L_\varepsilon\leq w(B^\star)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\leq w(B_\varepsilon)\leq U_\varepsilon. \tag{9}
\]
If \(C_-\) attains the minimum defining \(L_\varepsilon\), then (6) and \(B_{C_-}\in C_-\cap K_\kappa\) imply
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}leq w(B_{C_-})
\leq\overline w_{C_-}
\leq L_\varepsilon+\alpha.
\tag{10}
\]
Likewise, since \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\in I_w(C^\star)\),
\[
U_\varepsilon\leq\overline w_{C^\star}
\leq v_{\mathrm{mm}}+\alpha. \tag{11}
\]
Combining (10) and (11) yields
\[
U_\varepsilon-L_\varepsilon\leq2\alpha<\varepsilon. \tag{12}
\]

It remains to verify the outer-set certificate and the boundary rule.  At any stage, a valid box lower bound cannot exceed \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) on a box containing a minimizer, whereas every incumbent upper bound is at least \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\).  Therefore a box containing a minimizer is never removed by the strict pruning test
\(\underline w_C>U_\varepsilon\).  It is not removed by exact infeasibility either.  Hence the union \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\) of unpruned quotient-chart boxes satisfies
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_\varepsilon. \tag{13}
\]
Every retained box has diameter at most \(\varepsilon\), so
\[
h_\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon. \tag{14}
\]
In particular, a box meeting \(K_\kappa\) only on the equality boundary (7) is declared feasible by the exact decision oracle and cannot be discarded as infeasible; it can be discarded only through the valid objective-lower-bound test.  Equations (8)--(14), together with the recorded chart cover, interval calculations, point names, and pruning decisions, form the checkable certificate \(\mathscr K_\varepsilon\).

All required chart depths and arithmetic precisions are finite for the fixed input and are eventually reached by the stated refinement rule.  Thus its stopping tests are satisfied after finitely many subdivisions.  Finally, for any sequence \(\varepsilon_j\downarrow0\), the certificate inequalities give
\[
0\leq U_{\varepsilon_j}-L_{\varepsilon_j}\leq\varepsilon_j\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
0\leq h_{\varepsilon_j}\leq\varepsilon_j\longrightarrow0.
\]
The proof depends on the instance-specific refinement moduli and supplies neither a uniform subdivision bound nor a semidefinite-program reduction. \(\square\)

statements.statement: Let \(E_1,E_0\) be compact metric spaces.  Under weak convergence of an ordered pair of marginal probability measures, the fixed-marginal coupling correspondence is continuous in the weak topology.  Consequently, for every continuous function \(\varphi:E_1\times E_0\to\mathbb R\), the minimum and maximum of \(H\mapsto\int\varphi\,dH\) over the coupling set vary continuously with the ordered marginal pair, and the associated optimizer correspondences are upper hemicontinuous.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 1. Let X and Y be separable metrizable spaces and let φ : P(X) × P(Y) ⇉ P(X × Y) be defined: φ(μ,ν) = {τ ∈ P(X × Y) | τ_X = μ, τ_Y = ν}. The correspondence φ is continuous. According to Berge's maximum theorem, if W and Z are topological spaces and Φ : W ⇉ Z is a continuous correspondence with nonempty compact values, and f : W × Z → ℝ is continuous then (i) the function m(w) = max_{z∈Φ(w)} f(w,z) is continuous, and (ii) the correspondence β defined by β(w) = {z ∈ Z | f(w,z) = m(w)} is upper-hemicontinuous.
