Suppose ass:exposure-positivity holds and \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\).  If \(0<\kappa_1\le\kappa_2\) and both regular classes are nonempty, then
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}}w(B)
\le
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_2}}w(B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
=
\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
=
\inf_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}w(q_Z(B)).
\]
If the middle infimum is attained by some \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_Z\), then there is \(\kappa_0>0\) such that, for every \(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0\),
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
Thus the fixed-threshold values exhaust the entire maximal well-defined ordinary-inverse matrix domain in value through the quotient; singular or Moore--Penrose bases remain outside this conclusion.
statements.justification: This is the exact value transfer from fixed thresholds to the quotient and then to every ordinary-invertible matrix representative.
statements.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates does not introduce the normalized threshold family or prove value exhaustion and rescaling-fiber invariance.
statements.consumer: A solver can interpret its fixed-threshold optimum as an approximation to the best value over the full well-defined ordinary-inverse matrix domain.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
If \(0<\kappa_1\le\kappa_2\), then \(\mathcal B_{\kappa_2}\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}\), so minimizing the same continuous loss over the larger compact set proves the first inequality.  Prop:kappa-exhaustion gives \(\mathcal B_Z=\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa\).  The infimum of a function over a union is the infimum of the infima over its nonempty members, whence
\[
\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
=\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B). \tag{1}
\]
Thm:zhao-ordinary-domain-quotient-transfer makes \(q_Z\) surjective and shows that \(w(q_Z(B))\) is constant on every fiber.  Hence
\[
\inf_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}w(q_Z(B))
=\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B), \tag{2}
\]
which proves the full value equality.

If \(B_Z^\star\) attains the quotient infimum, prop:kappa-exhaustion supplies \(\kappa_0>0\) with \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_0}\).  For \(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0\),
\[
\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
\le\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
\le w(B_Z^\star)
=\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
This proves equality.  Equations (1)--(2) concern only ordinary-invertible matrices and their rescaling quotient. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Let \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\) be the maximal block-separable matrix domain on which the ordinary inverse in Zhao's Equation (8) is defined, and let \(q_Z(B)=[B]\).  Then \(q_Z:\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\to\mathcal B_Z\) is surjective, and
\[
q_Z(B)=q_Z(C)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
C=B\operatorname{diag}(t_1,t_0)
\quad\text{for some }t_1t_0\ne0.
\]
For every such diagonal \(T\), every \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), and every \(B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\),
\[
g_{q_Z(BT)}(c)=g_{q_Z(B)}(c),\qquad
\ell_{q_Z(BT)}(c)=\ell_{q_Z(B)}(c),\qquad
w(q_Z(BT))=w(q_Z(B)).
\]
Consequently, for every nonempty \(K\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\), the infima and suprema of each displayed pullback criterion over \(q_Z^{-1}(K)\) equal those over \(K\), and every attained argmin or argmax correspondence on the matrix domain is exactly the inverse image under \(q_Z\) of its quotient correspondence.  This is an exact quotient transfer for the ordinary-inverse domain implicit in Zhao's formula; it neither defines nor attributes a singular Moore--Penrose domain to Zhao.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
If \(B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\), then \(S_B\succ0\), so each arm column is nonzero and def:zhao-basis-class defines \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\).  Conversely, every \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\) has a block-separable representative with \(C^{\top}\Omega C\succ0\), hence a preimage in \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\).  Thus \(q_Z\) is onto.  The definition of the projective quotient says exactly that two representatives have the same class if and only if \(C=BT\) for a diagonal \(T=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,t_0)\) with \(t_1t_0\ne0\), proving the fiber formula.

For such \(T\),
\[
S_{BT}=T^{\top}S_BT,
\qquad
S_{BT}^{-1}=T^{-1}S_B^{-1}(T^{\top})^{-1}. \tag{1}
\]
Substitute (1) and \(BT\) into def:gain-loss.  Cyclicity of trace cancels \(T\) and \(T^{-1}\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
n^2g_{q_Z(BT)}(c)
&=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[T^{-1}S_B^{-1}(T^{\top})^{-1}
T^{\top}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega BT\right]\\
&=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right]
=n^2g_{q_Z(B)}(c).
\end{aligned}
\]
The uncontrolled term \(h(c)\) does not depend on \(B\), so the endpoint losses and their maximum are invariant as well.  An invariant function is constant on every fiber of a surjection.  Its image values over \(q_Z^{-1}(K)\) therefore equal its values over \(K\), proving equality of infima and suprema; if an extremum is attained, a matrix is an optimizer exactly when its quotient class is, giving the inverse-image correspondence. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Let \(\xi_0\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\) and suppose that, for some \(\eta>0\),
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}
\left\{\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\right\}\ge\eta.
\]
For every sequence \((\xi_j)_{j\ge1}\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) converging to \(\xi_0\) in the relative topology of def:lawful-instance-class,
\[
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta(\xi_j)\ge\Delta(\xi_0).
\]
statements.justification: This quantitative lower-semicontinuity lemma is the reusable step that turns an exact optimizer-wide slack certificate into a uniform dominance margin.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals supplies continuity of the fixed-marginal coupling correspondence; the new step propagates that continuity through the moving regular projective feasible set and both optimizer correspondences.
statements.consumer: The triangle neighborhood corollary uses the lemma to preserve half of the exact rational separation margin.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let \(\xi_j=(\nu_j,F_{1j},F_{0j})\to\xi_0\).  Use normalized representatives in the fixed compact product of the two radius-\(\sqrt n\) spheres modulo independent sign changes; this is the compact representation supplied by prop:kappa-exhaustion.  Because the assignment space is finite, total-variation convergence of \(\nu_j\) implies entrywise convergence
\[
\Pi_j\longrightarrow\Pi_0,
\qquad
\Omega_j\longrightarrow\Omega_0.                                    \tag{1}
\]
Exposure positivity at \(\xi_0\) implies that every relevant diagonal entry of \(\Pi_j\) is uniformly bounded away from zero for all sufficiently large \(j\), and hence
\[
\Pi_j^{-1}\longrightarrow\Pi_0^{-1}.                                \tag{2}
\]

Wasserstein convergence on \([0,1]\) implies weak convergence and convergence of first and second moments.  Apply lem:restricted-marginal-extrema-continuity with \(\varphi(y_1,y_0)=y_1y_0\).  The minimum and maximum cross moments over the coupling sets converge.  Subtracting the convergent products of marginal means yields
\[
c_{Lj}\longrightarrow c_{L0},
\qquad
c_{Uj}\longrightarrow c_{U0}.                                       \tag{3}
\]
Def:moment-matrix and convergence of the marginal first and second moments then give
\[
Q_j(c_{ej})\longrightarrow Q_0(c_{e0})
\qquad(e\in\{L,U\}).                                                \tag{4}
\]

For a normalized basis \(B\), put
\[
\rho(\xi,B)=\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega(\xi)B\}.
\]
This function is jointly continuous by (1).  On the closed region \(\rho\ge\kappa\), the inverse exists and satisfies
\[
\lVert S_B^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le(n\kappa)^{-1}.               \tag{5}
\]
Equations (1)--(5), def:gain-loss, and the endpoint reduction of thm:fixed-basis-endpoints show that \(g_{B,\xi}(0)\), both endpoint losses, and \(w_\xi(B)\) are jointly continuous on this region.

Choose \(B^\star_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\), which exists because ass:kappa-feasibility and prop:kappa-exhaustion make the feasible set nonempty and compact.  The assumed slack gives
\(\rho(\xi_0,B^\star_{\mathrm{mm}})\ge\kappa+\eta\), so this fixed representative is feasible for all sufficiently large \(j\).  Therefore
\[
\limsup_{j\to\infty}v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_j)
\le\lim_{j\to\infty}w_{\xi_j}(B^\star_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0).                                           \tag{6}
\]

For each \(j\), compactness and continuity allow a choice
\[
B_{0j}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B).
\]
Choose a subsequence that realizes the lower limit of these minimum values and, by compactness, a further subsequence such that \(B_{0j}\to\bar B_0\).  Closedness of the inequality \(\rho\ge\kappa\) makes \(\bar B_0\) feasible at \(\xi_0\).  Choose any \(C_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)\).  Its assumed slack makes it feasible for all sufficiently large \(j\), and the defining optimality of \(B_{0j}\) for the zero-covariance criterion gives
\[
g_{B_{0j},\xi_j}(0)\ge g_{C_0,\xi_j}(0).
\]
Passing to the limit shows \(g_{\bar B_0,\xi_0}(0)\ge g_{C_0,\xi_0}(0)\).  Since \(C_0\) already attains the feasible maximum and \(\bar B_0\) is feasible, equality holds and \(\bar B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)\).  Joint continuity now gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B)
&=w_{\xi_0}(\bar B_0)\\
&\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B).
\end{aligned}                                                       \tag{7}
\]
The subsequence was selected to realize the lower limit, so (7) holds for the original sequence.

Finally, def:dominance-gap, (6), (7), and the elementary inequality \(\liminf(a_j-b_j)\ge\liminf a_j-\limsup b_j\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta(\xi_j)
&\ge
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\\
&=\Delta(\xi_0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every division, inverse, moving-feasible-set comparison, and boundary passage is justified respectively by exposure positivity, the \(\kappa\)-bound, compactness, and the stated optimizer-wide slack. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For the explicit triangle instance \(\xi_0\) and \(\kappa=1/8\) in thm:triangle-minimax-separation-certificate, there is a relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) containing \(\xi_0\) such that
\[
\Delta(\xi)>\frac{\delta}{2}=\frac{2456}{39525}
\qquad(\xi\in\mathcal U),
\]
where \(\delta=4912/39525\).  Consequently, for every \(\xi\in\mathcal U\), every \(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\), and every \(B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)\),
\[
w_\xi(B_{\mathrm{mm}})<w_\xi(B_0).
\]
statements.justification: The explicit witness becomes a nondegenerate region of lawful designs and marginals, with a retained rational performance margin.
statements.gap: Neither Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates nor general dependence-robust optimization results give a strict full-correspondence comparison between the minimax and zero-covariance basis rules on an open family of network experiments.
statements.consumer: Nearby lawful network experiments inherit the guarantee that every minimax optimizer has lower worst-copula residual variance than every zero-covariance optimizer.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Thm:triangle-minimax-separation-certificate gives
\[
\Delta(\xi_0)=\delta=\frac{4912}{39525}>0
\]
and optimizer-wide slack \(\eta=5/216>0\).  Thm:relative-open-persistence first yields a relative-open neighborhood with positive gap.  To retain half the exact margin, suppose for contradiction that every relative-open neighborhood of \(\xi_0\) contained an instance with gap at most \(\delta/2\).  Metrizability then supplies a sequence \(\xi_j\to\xi_0\) with \(\Delta(\xi_j)\le\delta/2\).  Lem:dominance-gap-lower-semicontinuity would give
\[
\delta=\Delta(\xi_0)
\le\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta(\xi_j)
\le\frac\delta2,
\]
which is impossible.  Hence some relative-open \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) satisfies \(\Delta(\xi)>\delta/2=2456/39525\).

For any indicated optimizers, def:dominance-gap and the fact that every minimax optimizer has loss \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
w_\xi(B_0)-w_\xi(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
&\ge
\inf_{C_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)}w_\xi(C_0)
-\sup_{C\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)}w_\xi(C)\\
&=\Delta(\xi)>\frac\delta2>0.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the strict full-correspondence comparison. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Let \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\).  Under ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures, ass:exposure-positivity, ass:frechet-covariance-domain, and ass:product-coupling-zero,
\[
h(c)=h(0)+\frac{2c}{n}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
w(B)=h(0)+\max\left\{\frac{2c_L}{n}-g_B(c_L),\frac{2c_U}{n}-g_B(c_U)\right\}.
\]
If \(c_L<c_U\), minimization of \(w(B)\) is not algebraically equivalent to maximization of \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\): as functions of a formal endpoint-gain pair \((x_L,x_U)\), the two loss criteria are not related by a constant independent of \((x_L,x_U)\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let
\[
E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\ I_n&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}.
\]
The product-coupling assumption and the sharp covariance-domain assumption ensure that \(0\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), so \(Q(0)\) and \(h(0)\) are well typed.  From the definition of the moment matrix,
\[
Q(c)=Q(0)-cE
\qquad\text{for every }c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0).
\]

For each unit \(i\), mutual exclusivity gives \(D_{i,1}D_{i,0}=0\) almost surely.  Hence
\[
\Omega_{i,n+i}
=\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(D_{i,1},D_{i,0})
=\mathbb E_\nu[D_{i,1}D_{i,0}]-\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}
=-\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}.
\]
Exposure positivity permits division by both probabilities.  Since \(\Omega\), and therefore \(A_{\mathrm{HT}}\), is symmetric,
\[
\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}}E)
=2\sum_{i=1}^n(A_{\mathrm{HT}})_{i,n+i}
=2\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{\Omega_{i,n+i}}{\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}}
=-2n.
\]
Substitution into the trace definition of \(h\) yields, for every feasible \(c\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
h(c)
&=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left\{A_{\mathrm{HT}}Q(c)\right\}\\
&=h(0)-cn^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}}E)\\
&=h(0)+\frac{2c}{n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Using \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\) at \(c_L\) and \(c_U\), followed by the definition of \(w\), gives
\[
w(B)=h(0)+\max\left\{\frac{2c_L}{n}-g_B(c_L),\frac{2c_U}{n}-g_B(c_U)\right\}.
\]

It remains to verify the claimed algebraic non-equivalence.  Assume \(c_L<c_U\), put \(a_e=2c_e/n\), and for a formal nonnegative endpoint-gain pair \(x=(x_L,x_U)\) define
\[
\Phi(x)=\max\{a_L-x_L,a_U-x_U\},
\qquad
\Psi(x)=-\min\{x_L,x_U\}.
\]
If the two criteria differed by a constant independent of \(x\), there would be a \(K\) such that \(\Phi(x)=\Psi(x)+K\) for every \(x\).  At \(x=(t,0)\) with \(t\ge0\), one has \(\Psi(x)=0\) and, because \(a_L<a_U\), \(\Phi(x)=a_U\); hence \(K=a_U\).  At \(x=(0,t)\) with \(t\ge a_U-a_L\), one has \(\Psi(x)=0\) and \(\Phi(x)=a_L\); hence \(K=a_L\).  This contradicts \(a_L<a_U\).  Therefore minimization of the endpoint-drift-adjusted residual criterion is not algebraically equivalent to maximization of the minimum endpoint gain. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Suppose ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility hold.  The primary minimax correspondence is nonempty and satisfies the unconditional weak worst-copula dominance certificate
\[
\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}}w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0).
\]
Strict inequality is not universal and requires a separate lawful witness.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
By the \(\kappa\)-feasibility assumption, \(\mathcal B_\kappa\neq\varnothing\).  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}kappa\mbox{-}exhaustion}\) gives compactness of \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) and the inclusion \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\).  Hence all ordinary inverses appearing below are well defined.

We first verify attainment from the primitive design conditions.  Exposure positivity gives an invertible diagonal matrix \(\Pi\).  Every normalized representative of an element of \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) satisfies
\[
S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\succeq n\kappa I_2,
\]
so \(B\mapsto S_B^{-1}\) is continuous and uniformly bounded on the normalized representative set.  For each fixed \(e\in\{L,U\}\), the matrix
\[
M_e=\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega
\]
is fixed and finite, and therefore
\[
g_B(c_e)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left(S_B^{-1}B^{\top}M_eB\right)
\]
is continuous in a normalized representative.  The formula is invariant under the residual independent sign changes of the two normalized columns, so it descends continuously to the projective quotient \(\mathcal B_\kappa\).  The same argument applies to \(g_B(0)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}ht\mbox{-}affine\mbox{-}drift}\),
\[
w(B)=h(0)+\max\left\{\frac{2c_L}{n}-g_B(c_L),\frac{2c_U}{n}-g_B(c_U)\right\},
\]
and thus \(w\) is continuous as the maximum of two continuous functions.  The Weierstrass theorem on the nonempty compact set \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) now shows that both
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathcal A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)
\]
are nonempty.

For arbitrary \(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(B_0\in\mathcal A_0\), the definition of the minimum gives
\[
w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_0).
\]
Every member of \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) has loss exactly \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\).  Taking the supremum over \(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and then the infimum over \(B_0\) therefore yields
\[
\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}}w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0).
\]

Finally, strictness cannot be asserted uniformly over lawful instances.  Fix any design satisfying exposure positivity and \(\kappa\)-feasibility, and take the lawful bounded marginals \(F_1=F_0=\delta_0\).  Then \(\mu_1=\mu_0=\sigma_1^2=\sigma_0^2=0\), the two sharp covariance endpoints are \(c_L=c_U=0\), and
\[
Q(0)=0.
\]
Consequently \(h(0)=g_B(0)=\ell_B(0)=w(B)=0\) for every \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\).  Both optimizer correspondences equal the whole feasible class and the displayed weak inequality is an equality.  Thus a separate lawful witness is necessary for strict dominance. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For every rational signed pivot-chart box, intersection with the normalized feasible set \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is an existential semialgebraic question.  More explicitly, sphere feasibility, chart and box restrictions, and \(S_B-n\kappa I_2\succeq0\) are finitely many polynomial equalities and weak inequalities with rational or real-algebraic coefficients; for
\[
 S_B-n\kappa I_2=\begin{bmatrix}u&v\\v&z\end{bmatrix},
\]
the matrix inequality is exactly \(u\ge0\), \(z\ge0\), and \(uz-v^2\ge0\).  Cylindrical algebraic decomposition therefore terminates with either an exact real-algebraic feasible sample or a finite infeasibility certificate, including when feasibility occurs only on the equality boundary.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix a rational signed pivot-chart box and write the \(2n\) coordinates of \((b_1,b_0)\) as \(x\).  The normalization conditions are the polynomial equations
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n b_{1i}^2=n,
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^n b_{0i}^2=n.
\]
Every box restriction and signed pivot restriction is a polynomial weak inequality with rational coefficients.  Because \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), every entry of \(S_B\) is a quadratic polynomial in \(x\) with rational or real-algebraic coefficients.

Write
\[
S_B-n\kappa I_2=
\begin{bmatrix}u&v\\v&z\end{bmatrix}.
\]
If this matrix is positive semidefinite, its one-by-one and two-by-two principal minors give
\[
u\ge0,\qquad z\ge0,\qquad uz-v^2\ge0. \tag{1}
\]
Conversely, suppose (1) holds.  If \(u>0\), then for every \((s,t)\in\mathbb R^2\),
\[
us^2+2vst+zt^2
=u\left(s+\frac vu t\right)^2
+\left(z-\frac{v^2}{u}\right)t^2\ge0.
\]
If \(u=0\), the determinant inequality forces \(v=0\), and the quadratic form equals \(zt^2\ge0\).  Thus (1) is also sufficient.  In particular, it retains rather than discards the equality boundary.

Intersection of the chart box with the normalized feasible set is therefore expressed by one existential first-order formula
\[
\exists x\;\Phi(x),
\]
where \(\Phi\) is a finite conjunction of polynomial equalities and weak inequalities over the real-algebraic coefficient field.  By lem:real-closed-field-quantifier-elimination, Collins's EVAL/ELIM construction returns after finitely many eliminations a quantifier-free formula equivalent to this existential formula.  Exact real-algebraic sign isolation decides the returned formula.

For completeness, the witness part of the same cylindrical construction is obtained during lifting.  At each of the finitely many lifting levels, the projection polynomials specialize to finitely many univariate polynomials with real-algebraic coefficients.  Exact root isolation partitions the line into finitely many open sectors and root sections; choosing a rational point in a sector or the isolated real-algebraic root in a section gives an algebraic sample.  The number of variables, projection polynomials, roots, and resulting cells is finite, so recursive lifting terminates.  A cell whose sign vector satisfies \(\Phi\) returns its real-algebraic sample.  If no cell satisfies \(\Phi\), the finite sign-invariant cell list together with the quantifier-elimination trace is an infeasibility certificate.  Since weak inequalities admit root sections, the conclusion remains valid when all feasible samples lie on the sphere or \(\kappa\)-equality boundary. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For every rational or real-algebraic input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility, and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), the algebraic projective interval branch-and-bound procedure terminates after finitely many subdivisions and returns a locally checkable certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) such that
\[
 L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon},
 \qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
 \qquad h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
 \qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\varepsilon}.
\]
The incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\) has finite real-algebraic coordinates, including when every feasible point lies on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  The checker verifies only CAD sign certificates, algebraic feasibility, outward objective bounds, rational norm and diameter records, chart cover, pruning inequalities, and mesh; the displayed facts about \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) are mathematical consequences.  Along every \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and meshes converge to zero.  No uniform complexity bound or semidefinite-program reduction is asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Write \(c_e=c_L\) for \(e=L\) and \(c_e=c_U\) for \(e=U\).

\emph{Step 1: compact algebraic feasibility, including the boundary.}
For normalized representatives put
\[
K_\kappa=
\left\{(b_1,b_0):
\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n,
\quad S_B-n\kappa I_2\succeq0
\right\}.
\]
Assumption ass:kappa-feasibility makes \(K_\kappa\) nonempty.  It is a closed subset of the product of two radius-\(\sqrt n\) spheres, hence compact.  Proposition prop:kappa-exhaustion identifies its projective quotient with the compact class \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) and gives \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\).  Every feasible representative therefore satisfies
\[
S_B\succeq n\kappa I_2\succ0. \tag{1}
\]
Thus every ordinary inverse in \(w(B)\) exists even at
\(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)=\kappa\).

On a radius-\(\sqrt n\) sphere at least one coordinate has absolute value at least one.  The finitely many signed pivot regions \(\{b_j\ge1\}\) and \(\{-b_j\ge1\}\), applied to each arm factor, cover the normalized projective domain.  Finite rational boxes in these charts, together with the two sphere equations, give a finite initial cover.  Lemma lem:algebraic-box-feasibility-cad decides exactly whether each box intersects \(K_\kappa\).  A nonempty intersection yields a real-algebraic feasible point even when the intersection is contained in the equality boundary in (1); an empty intersection yields a finite CAD infeasibility certificate.

\emph{Step 2: an effective uniform modulus for the endpoint loss.}
For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), define
\[
R_e=\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega,
\qquad S(B)=B^{\top}\Omega B,
\qquad T_e(B)=B^{\top}R_eB.
\]
The input entries are rational or real algebraic.  Assumption ass:exposure-positivity makes \(\Pi\) invertible, and exact algebraic sign isolation verifies that fact.  Algebraic-number isolation supplies rational bounds
\[
M_\Omega\ge\lVert\Omega\rVert_2,
\qquad M_e\ge\lVert R_e\rVert_2.
\]
Every normalized block matrix has \(\lVert B\rVert_F=\sqrt{2n}\).  Hence, for feasible normalized representatives \(B,C\), with \(d=\lVert B-C\rVert_F\), the identity
\[
B^{\top}AB-C^{\top}AC
=(B-C)^{\top}AB+C^{\top}A(B-C)
\]
and submultiplicativity give
\[
\lVert S(B)-S(C)\rVert_2\le K_Sd,
\qquad
\lVert T_e(B)-T_e(C)\rVert_2\le K_{T,e}d, \tag{2}
\]
where one may take
\[
K_S=2\sqrt{2n}\,M_\Omega,
\qquad K_{T,e}=2\sqrt{2n}\,M_e.
\]
By (1), \(\lVert S(B)^{-1}\rVert_2\le(n\kappa)^{-1}\).  The resolvent identity gives
\[
\lVert S(B)^{-1}-S(C)^{-1}\rVert_2
\le(n\kappa)^{-2}K_Sd. \tag{3}
\]
Also \(\lVert T_e(C)\rVert_2\le2nM_e\).  Using
\(\lvert\operatorname{tr}(XY)\rvert\le2\lVert X\rVert_2\lVert Y\rVert_2\)
for two-by-two matrices, (2)--(3), and
\[
S(B)^{-1}T_e(B)-S(C)^{-1}T_e(C)
=S(B)^{-1}\{T_e(B)-T_e(C)\}
+\{S(B)^{-1}-S(C)^{-1}\}T_e(C),
\]
we obtain
\[
\lvert g_B(c_e)-g_C(c_e)\rvert\le L_ed,
\quad
L_e=n^{-2}\left\{
\frac{2K_{T,e}}{n\kappa}
+\frac{4nM_eK_S}{(n\kappa)^2}
\right\}. \tag{4}
\]
The uncontrolled term \(h(c_e)\) is independent of \(B\), and the maximum of two real numbers is one-Lipschitz in the sup norm.  Therefore
\[
\lvert w(B)-w(C)\rvert
\le L\lVert B-C\rVert_F,
\qquad L=\max\{L_L,L_U\}. \tag{5}
\]
Every quantity in (4) is effectively bounded from the algebraic input, so algebraic isolation returns and records a rational \(\overline L\ge L\).

\emph{Step 3: finite subdivision and the value certificate.}
Because \(\varepsilon>0\) is exactly encoded, algebraic isolation returns a rational \(\rho>0\) with \(4\rho<\varepsilon\).  Uniform bisection of the finite chart cover reaches, after finitely many subdivisions, a depth at which every box \(C\) has a recorded rational representative-coordinate diameter \(d_C\) satisfying
\[
d_C\le\varepsilon,
\qquad \overline Ld_C\le\rho. \tag{6}
\]
There are finitely many boxes at that depth.  The CAD lemma supplies an exact infeasibility certificate for each empty box and a real-algebraic point \(B_C\in C\cap K_\kappa\) for each nonempty box.  Since \(w(B_C)\) is the maximum of two real-algebraic numbers, outward algebraic isolation terminates with rationals \(\underline q_C,\overline q_C\) such that
\[
w(B_C)-\rho\le\underline q_C\le w(B_C)
\le\overline q_C\le w(B_C)+\rho. \tag{7}
\]
For a feasible box define
\[
\lambda_C=\underline q_C-\overline Ld_C.
\]
Equations (5)--(7) imply the certified box lower bound
\[
\lambda_C\le\inf_{B\in C\cap K_\kappa}w(B). \tag{8}
\]
Set
\[
U_\varepsilon=\min_C\overline q_C,
\qquad L_\varepsilon=\min_C\lambda_C,
\]
where both minima range over feasible boxes, and choose \(B_\varepsilon\) to be the real-algebraic sample attaining the first minimum.  Compactness and (5) give a minimizer \(B^\star\).  For every feasible \(C\), (6)--(7) imply
\[
\lambda_C\ge w(B_C)-2\rho\ge v_{\mathrm{mm}}-2\rho.
\]
For a box containing \(B^\star\), the same displays imply
\[
\overline q_C\le w(B_C)+\rho
\le w(B^\star)+2\rho=v_{\mathrm{mm}}+2\rho.
\]
Combining these inequalities with (8) and feasibility of the incumbent gives
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}-2\rho
\le L_\varepsilon\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le w(B_\varepsilon)\le U_\varepsilon
\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}+2\rho,
\]
and hence
\[
U_\varepsilon-L_\varepsilon\le4\rho<\varepsilon. \tag{9}
\]
This is a permitted instance of def:branch-bound-handle: the procedure may first make the uniform finite refinement just constructed and then apply objective pruning.  Thus the stopping tests are reached after finitely many subdivisions.

\emph{Step 4: outer minimizers and local checking.}
Prune an exactly feasible box by its objective only when \(\lambda_C>U_\varepsilon\).  By (8), no such box contains a global minimizer, because a box containing a minimizer satisfies
\[
\lambda_C\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le U_\varepsilon.
\]
Let \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\) be the union of the quotient images of all unpruned feasible boxes.  Then
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_\varepsilon.
\]
The quotient-chart metric is computed from normalized representative coordinates, so (6) also yields \(h_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon\).

The certificate contains only the finite chart cover, CAD sign and feasibility records, the algebraic incumbent, outward rational loss bounds, rational norm and diameter bounds, pruning comparisons, and the mesh.  A local checker verifies those records.  Compactness, (5), (8), and the pruning implication then prove the displayed assertions involving the unknown mathematical objects \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\); those assertions are not checker premises.  Boundary-only feasibility is covered by the weak polynomial inequalities and exact CAD samples in Step 1.  Finally, for every sequence \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), (9) and \(h_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon\) force both certificate gaps and meshes to converge to zero.

The comparison with Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates is objective-specific.  Zhao's published network-interference result supplies a one-half approximation for its constrained gain problem and then uses an alternating search that converges only to a local maximum.  The present construction instead certifies an \(\varepsilon\)-global minimum of the endpoint worst-residual criterion \(w\) on the fixed normalized \(\kappa\)-regular class.  The objectives and feasible classes are not asserted to coincide, and the proof gives neither a uniform complexity improvement nor a semidefinite-program reduction. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Suppose ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility, ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate, ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate, ass:zhao-first-order-rate, ass:bounded-outcomes, and ass:iid-potential-pairs hold.  Uniformly over the nonempty class \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), let
\[
\gamma_B^*(Y)=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y
\]
and let \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\) be the control-variate estimator using this fixed-array oracle coefficient.  There are finite constants \(K_\Delta,K_{\mathrm{cov}},K_R\), independent of \(n\), \(B\), the bounded array \(Y\), and \(H\), such that the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope
\[
R_n=K_\Delta n^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
+2K_{\mathrm{cov}}n^{(7/2)\alpha+3\beta-2},
\qquad K_R=K_\Delta+2K_{\mathrm{cov}},
\]
satisfies, for every \(n\ge3\),
\[
0\le R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
and the two uniform absolute bounds
\[
\sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\0\le Y_i(a)\le1}}
\left|
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
\right|
\le R_n,
\]
\[
\sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}}
\left|
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\ell_B(c_H)
\right|
\le R_n.
\]
The oracle ex ante identity is exact:
\[
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
=\ell_B(c_H),
\qquad
c_H=\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}.
\]
Since \(4\alpha+4\beta<1\), one has \(nR_n\to0\); hence the feasible and oracle conditional design variances differ by \(o(n^{-1})\), and the feasible ex ante variance equals \(\ell_B(c_H)+o(n^{-1})\), uniformly over the rate-admissible class.  The expectations over \(H^{\otimes n}\) are ex ante basis-performance averages, not additional randomness in the conditional design-based estimand.
statements.justification: This is the quantitative feasible-estimator bridge: it gives a deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope for the difference between Zhao's observable Horvitz--Thompson coefficient and the oracle coefficient, uniformly over the nonempty rate-admissible class.
statements.gap: The proof adapts Zhao's fixed-basis variance-equivalence regime uniformly over a class whose coordinate envelope and nonemptiness are imposed explicitly and supplies the public finite-\(n\) remainder \(R_n\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Assumption ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility makes \(\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\) nonempty.  Index the \(2n\) exposure coordinates by \(j\), write \(\pi_j=\mathbb E_\nu D_j\), and put \(Z_j=D_j-\pi_j\).  Thus \(|Z_j|\leq1\) and \(\mathbb E_\nu Z_j=0\).  Let \(N=2n\) and let \(d_n^{\mathrm{dep}}\leq\overline d n^\alpha\) be the maximum closed-neighborhood size in \(\mathcal G_n\).

We first record the dependency-graph counts used below.  In the expansion of a joint moment of centered coordinates, a tuple contributes zero whenever one of its distinct indices has no dependency edge to any other index in the tuple.  A contributing ordered four-tuple either contains two disjoint dependency edges, of which there are at most \(C N^2(d_n^{\mathrm{dep}})^2\), or its distinct-index dependency subgraph is connected, of which there are at most \(C N(d_n^{\mathrm{dep}})^3\le C N^2(d_n^{\mathrm{dep}})^2\).  Every contributing ordered three-tuple is connected after repeated indices are represented by closed-neighborhood edges, so there are at most \(C N(d_n^{\mathrm{dep}})^2\) of them.  Consequently, for deterministic scalar coefficient arrays \(q,r,s\),
\[
 \mathbb E_\nu\!\left(\sum_jq_jZ_j\right)^4
 \leq C N^2(d_n^{\mathrm{dep}})^2\lVert q\rVert_\infty^4,
 \tag{1}
\]
and
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_\nu
 \left(\sum_jq_jZ_j\right)
 \left(\sum_jr_jZ_j\right)
 \left(\sum_js_jZ_j\right)\right|
 \leq C N(d_n^{\mathrm{dep}})^2
 \lVert q\rVert_\infty\lVert r\rVert_\infty\lVert s\rVert_\infty.
 \tag{2}
\]
These inequalities follow directly by expansion, the preceding vanishing argument, \(|Z_j|\leq1\), and the tuple counts; hence no normal approximation is being assumed.

Fix a bounded potential-outcome array and \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\).  Write \(S_B=B^\top\Omega B\), so \(S_B\succeq n\kappa I_2\).  With \(Y_j\) denoting the signed coordinate of \(Y\), the definition of the observable stack gives
\[
 \{\Pi^{-1}(\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}-Y)\}_j
 =\frac{Y_jZ_j}{\pi_j^2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 G_B:=\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)-\gamma_B^*(Y)
 =\sum_{j=1}^{N}u_{B,j}Z_j,
 \qquad
 u_{B,j}=S_B^{-1}B^\top\Omega e_j\frac{Y_j}{\pi_j^2}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Every column of \(\Omega\) has at most \(d_n^{\mathrm{dep}}\) nonzero entries, each of absolute value at most one.  The coordinate envelope, exposure-rate bound, and \(\lVert S_B^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq(n\kappa)^{-1}\) thus imply
\[
 \sup_{B,j}\lVert u_{B,j}\rVert_2
 \leq K_u n^{\alpha+2\beta-1},
 \qquad
 K_u=\frac{\sqrt2\,\overline a\,\overline d}{\kappa\underline\pi^2}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Also set
\[
 X_B=n^{-1}B^\top(D-\mathbb E_\nu D)
 =\sum_{j=1}^{N}x_{B,j}Z_j,
 \qquad
 \sup_{B,j}\lVert x_{B,j}\rVert_2\leq\frac{\overline a}{n}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Applying (1) coordinatewise to (3)--(5), and absorbing the fixed dimension two into constants, gives
\[
 \sup_B\mathbb E_\nu\lVert G_B\rVert_2^4
 \leq K_G n^{6\alpha+8\beta-2},
 \qquad
 \sup_B\mathbb E_\nu\lVert X_B\rVert_2^4
 \leq K_X n^{2\alpha-2}.
 \tag{6}
\]
The feasible and oracle estimators obey
\[
 \widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
 =\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}+\Delta_B,
 \qquad
 \Delta_B=-G_B^\top X_B.
 \tag{7}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz and (6) yield the finite bound
\[
 \sup_B\mathbb E_\nu\Delta_B^2
 \leq K_\Delta n^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}.
 \tag{8}
\]

It remains to control the covariance term without replacing it by an unjustified absolute-third-moment count.  Put \(T_B=\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}-\tau\).  The Horvitz--Thompson term is unbiased and the oracle control statistic is centered, so \(\mathbb E_\nu T_B=0\).  Moreover
\[
 T_B=\sum_{j=1}^{N}t_{B,j}Z_j,
 \qquad
 t_{B,j}=n^{-1}\left\{\frac{Y_j}{\pi_j}-B_{j\cdot}\gamma_B^*(Y)\right\}.
 \tag{9}
\]
For \(Z_B=\Omega^{1/2}B\), the matrix \(Z_B(Z_B^\top Z_B)^{-1}Z_B^\top\) is an orthogonal projector.  Hence
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \gamma_B^*(Y)^\top S_B\gamma_B^*(Y)
 &=Y^\top\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^{-1}B^\top\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y\\
 &\leq Y^\top\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{10}
\]
The row-sparsity bound gives \(\lVert\Omega\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\overline d n^\alpha\), while bounded outcomes and exposure positivity give \(\lVert\Pi^{-1}Y\rVert_2^2\leq2\underline\pi^{-2}n^{1+2\beta}\).  Combining these facts with \(S_B\succeq n\kappa I_2\) in (10) proves
\[
 \sup_B\lVert\gamma_B^*(Y)\rVert_2
 \leq K_\gamma n^{\alpha/2+\beta}.
 \tag{11}
\]
Equations (9), (11), the coordinate envelope, and \(n\geq3\) then imply
\[
 \sup_{B,j}|t_{B,j}|
 \leq K_t n^{\alpha/2+\beta-1}.
 \tag{12}
\]
Using (3), (5), and (9), and the fact that \(T_B\) is centered, we may expand the covariance exactly as
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_\nu(T_B,\Delta_B\mid Y)
 =-\sum_{l=1}^{2}\sum_{i,j,k=1}^{N}
 t_{B,i}u_{B,j,l}x_{B,k,l}\,
 \mathbb E_\nu(Z_iZ_jZ_k).
 \tag{13}
\]
Applying the connected-triple bound (2) to (13), followed by (4), (5), and (12), gives
\[
 \sup_B\left|\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(T_B,\Delta_B\mid Y)\right|
 \leq K_{\mathrm{cov}}n^{(7/2)\alpha+3\beta-2}.
 \tag{14}
\]
This direct signed-moment calculation is the required covariance control.

Define the nonnegative, deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope
\[
 R_n
 :=K_\Delta n^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
 +2K_{\mathrm{cov}}n^{(7/2)\alpha+3\beta-2}.
 \tag{15}
\]
Because \(\alpha,\beta\geq0\),
\[
 \frac{7}{2}\alpha+3\beta
 \leq4\alpha+4\beta.
 \tag{16}
\]
Thus, for \(K_R=K_\Delta+2K_{\mathrm{cov}}\) and every \(n\geq3\),
\[
 R_n\leq K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}.
 \tag{17}
\]
Expanding the variance in (7), using \(\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\Delta_B\mid Y)\leq\mathbb E_\nu\Delta_B^2\), and applying (8) and (14), we obtain the uniform finite-sample certificate
\[
 \sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\0\leq Y_i(a)\leq1}}
 \left|
 \operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
 -\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
 \right|
 \leq R_n.
 \tag{18}
\]
Assumption ass:zhao-first-order-rate states \(4\alpha+4\beta<1\).  Therefore (17) gives \(nR_n\leq K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-1}\to0\), proving the first asymptotic assertion.

For the exact oracle identity, completing the square gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
 =n^{-2}Y^\top
 \left\{
 \Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}
 -\Pi^{-1}\Omega BS_B^{-1}B^\top\Omega\Pi^{-1}
 \right\}Y.
 \tag{19}
\]
Under ass:iid-potential-pairs, \(\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}(YY^\top)=Q(c_H)\).  Taking expectation in (19), using \(\mathbb E(Y^\top MY)=\operatorname{tr}\{M\mathbb E(YY^\top)\}\), and invoking def:gain-loss yields
\[
 \mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
 \operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
 =h(c_H)-g_B(c_H)=\ell_B(c_H).
 \tag{20}
\]
Finally, integrating (18) under \(H^{\otimes n}\) and applying (20) produces the finite ex ante envelope
\[
 \sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}}
 \left|
 \mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
 \operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
 -\ell_B(c_H)
 \right|
 \leq R_n=o(n^{-1}).
 \tag{21}
\]
The inner variance throughout is design based, conditional on the fixed array; the expectation in (20)--(21) is only the declared ex ante evaluation.  This proves every assertion. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Along a triangular sequence satisfying ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility, ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate, and ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate, let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the two endpoint matrices obtained from the unpaired empirical marginals, and put
\[
C_n=n^{-2}\left[
\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\rVert_*
+\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\right].
\]
Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot,
\[
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
=O_{L^1}\!\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}\right),
\qquad
C_n=O\!\left(n^{\alpha+2\beta-1}\right).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|
\le C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Writing \(\widehat Q(0)\) for the zero-covariance moment matrix formed from the empirical marginal moments, one also has
\[
\lVert\widehat Q(0)-Q(0)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\]
and therefore
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|
\le 2n^{-2}\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Hence the exact sensitivity condition
\[
nC_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{in }L^1
\]
implies uniform first-order plug-in accuracy for both criteria.  A sufficient bounded-pilot condition is
\[
\frac{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}{n^{1+\alpha+2\beta}}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
statements.justification: This lemma derives the pilot-size requirement needed to make robust and zero-covariance basis selection accurate on the first-order design-variance scale over a nonempty rate class.
statements.gap: The explicit factor-two matrix comparison prevents endpoint covariance error from being silently reused as a zero-covariance moment-matrix bound.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Assumption ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility makes the rate-admissible class nonempty.  Put \(m=m_1\wedge m_0\).  We first control the empirical marginal functionals.  For probability laws \(R,S\) on \([0,1]\), the one-dimensional area identity gives
\[
\int_0^1|R^{-1}(u)-S^{-1}(u)|\,du
=\int_0^1|R(y)-S(y)|\,dy.
\tag{1}
\]
Indeed, both sides are the Lebesgue area of the symmetric difference between the two subgraphs.  For each empirical distribution function, Jensen's inequality and the binomial variance formula yield
\[
\mathbb E_P|\widehat F_a(y)-F_a(y)|
\le \sqrt{\frac{F_a(y)\{1-F_a(y)\}}{m_a}}
\le \frac{1}{2\sqrt{m_a}}.
\]
Integrating and using (1) gives
\[
\mathbb E_P W_1(\widehat F_a,F_a)\le \frac{1}{2\sqrt{m_a}}.
\tag{2}
\]
The functions \(y\mapsto y\) and \(y\mapsto y^2\) are Lipschitz on \([0,1]\).  Hence the empirical means, second moments, and variances all have \(L^1(P)\) error of order \(m_a^{-1/2}\).

For \(x,x',y,y'\in[0,1]\),
\[
|xy-x'y'|\le |x-x'|+|y-y'|.
\tag{3}
\]
Apply (3) to the empirical and population quantile functions.  The comonotone product integrals differ by at most
\[
W_1(\widehat F_1,F_1)+W_1(\widehat F_0,F_0).
\]
Replacing the second quantile argument by \(1-u\) proves the same bound for the countermonotone product integral.  Combining these bounds with the empirical mean-product error gives, for \(e\in\{L,U\}\),
\[
|\widehat c_e-c_e|+
\sum_{a\in\{1,0\}}
\bigl(|\widehat\mu_a-\mu_a|+|\widehat\sigma_a^2-\sigma_a^2|\bigr)
=O_{L^1}(m^{-1/2}).
\tag{4}
\]
Every block of \(\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\) is a scalar appearing in (4) times either \(I_n\) or \(\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top}\).  Their operator norms are \(1\) and \(n\), respectively.  Thus
\[
M_n:=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}
\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
=O_{L^1}\!\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt m}\right).
\tag{5}
\]

Next define
\[
A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1},
\qquad
A_B=\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}.
\tag{6}
\]
For \(Z=\Omega^{1/2}B\), the matrix
\[
P_Z=Z(Z^{\top}Z)^{-1}Z^{\top}
\]
is an orthogonal projector because every \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\) has \(B^{\top}\Omega B\succ0\).  Consequently
\[
0\preceq A_B
=\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}P_Z\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}
\preceq A_{\mathrm{HT}}.
\tag{7}
\]
The nuclear norm of a positive semidefinite matrix is its trace, so (7) implies
\[
\lVert A_B\rVert_*\le\lVert A_{\mathrm{HT}}\rVert_*.
\tag{8}
\]
The dependency-graph condition makes every row of \(\Omega\) have at most \(\overline d n^\alpha\) possibly nonzero entries: two distinct nonadjacent coordinates are independent and therefore have covariance zero.  Since the coordinates are indicators, every covariance has absolute value at most one.  The exposure-rate condition also gives
\[
\lVert\Pi^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\underline\pi^{-1}n^\beta.
\]
The maximum-row-sum bound and the fact that \(A_{\mathrm{HT}}\) is a \(2n\)-dimensional positive semidefinite matrix therefore give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\lVert A_{\mathrm{HT}}\rVert_*
&\le2n\lVert A_{\mathrm{HT}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\\
&\le2\overline d\,\underline\pi^{-2}
n^{1+\alpha+2\beta}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
Equations (8)--(9) prove
\[
C_n=O(n^{\alpha+2\beta-1}).
\tag{10}
\]

Trace duality applied to (6) gives, for each endpoint,
\[
|\widehat h_e-h_e|
\le n^{-2}\lVert A_{\mathrm{HT}}\rVert_*M_n,
\qquad
|\widehat g_B(c_e)-g_B(c_e)|
\le n^{-2}\lVert A_B\rVert_*M_n.
\tag{11}
\]
The map \((x_L,x_U)\mapsto\max\{x_L,x_U\}\) is one-Lipschitz in the maximum norm.  Since \(\ell_B=h-g_B\), (11) and the definition of \(C_n\) imply
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|\le C_nM_n.
\tag{12}
\]

It remains to control the zero-covariance plug-in matrix rather than silently substituting an endpoint bound.  Let \(\widehat Q(0)\) be formed from the empirical means and variances with covariance set to zero, put
\[
\Delta_0=\widehat Q(0)-Q(0),
\qquad
\Delta_e=\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e),
\qquad
d_e=\widehat c_e-c_e,
\]
and define the exchange matrix
\[
E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\I_n&0\end{bmatrix}.
\]
The affine moment-matrix identity, applied once to the empirical marginals and once to the population marginals, gives
\[
\Delta_0=\Delta_e+d_eE.
\tag{13}
\]
The upper-right \(n\)-by-\(n\) block of \(\Delta_e\) is
\[
-\bigl(\widehat\mu_1\widehat\mu_0-\mu_1\mu_0\bigr)
\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top}-d_eI_n.
\tag{14}
\]
Because \(n\ge3\), choose a unit vector \(z\perp\mathbf1\).  The matrix in (14) sends \(z\) to \(-d_ez\).  A block compression cannot have larger operator norm than its parent matrix, and hence
\[
|d_e|\le\lVert\Delta_e\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{15}
\]
Since \(\lVert E\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=1\), (13)--(15) show
\[
\lVert\Delta_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\lVert\Delta_e\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2M_n.
\tag{16}
\]
Trace duality at zero covariance now proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_B|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|
&\le n^{-2}\sup_B\lVert A_B\rVert_*
\lVert\Delta_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\\
&\le2n^{-2}\sup_B\lVert A_B\rVert_*M_n
\le2C_nM_n.
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
Thus the exact sensitivity condition makes \(n\) times both uniform errors converge to zero in \(L^1(P)\).  Finally, (5) and (10) give
\[
nC_nM_n
=O_{L^1}\!\left(
\frac{n^{1+\alpha+2\beta}}{\sqrt m}
\right),
\]
which tends to zero under the displayed pilot-growth condition.  This proves every assertion. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Suppose ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility holds.  Under the assumptions of lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, suppose ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence and the exact sensitivity condition hold, and use the independent-pilot selectors of def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator.  Put
\[
M_n=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
\[
d_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|,
\qquad
e_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|.
\]
For every \(n\), almost surely under the pilot law,
\[
d_n\le C_nM_n,
\qquad e_n\le2C_nM_n.
\]
Write
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}w(B),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0).
\]
Then the robust selector obeys the finite pilot-regret inequality
\[
0\le
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})-v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}
\le2C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
\]
Let \(R_n\) be the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, and, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\), define
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
The feasible-estimator bridge is the finite bound
\[
|V_s-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)|\le R_n,
\qquad s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}.
\]
The exact sensitivity condition implies
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+o(n^{-1}),
\qquad
V_s=\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)+o(n^{-1}).
\]
In addition, define
\[
g_n^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0),
\qquad
q_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B).
\]
If there are deterministic \(L_n\in[0,\infty)\) with \(\sup_nL_n<\infty\) such that, for every \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\),
\[
[q_n-w(B)]_+\le L_n\{g_n^\star-g_B(0)\},
\]
then the finite zero-surrogate inequality
\[
q_n-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\le4L_nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n
\]
holds, and consequently
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B)-o(n^{-1}).
\]
The linear error bound is a deterministic geometric property of the two ordinary-domain objective surfaces.  Without it, ordinary outer argmax consistency alone is only \(o(1)\) and does not justify a first-order \(o(n^{-1})\) ordering.
statements.justification: This theorem derives nonempty measurable pilot selectors, finite pilot-selection regret, and a deterministic feasible-estimator variance bridge before taking the first-order limit.
statements.gap: The zero-surrogate finite-\(n\) conclusion uses a bounded deterministic linear error bound between nominal-gain regret and worst-loss deficit; outer argmax consistency alone is insufficient on the \(n^{-1}\) scale.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Write \(\mathcal K_n=\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\).  Assumption ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility gives \(\mathcal K_n\ne\varnothing\).  Its normalized representatives form a closed subset of the product of two radius-\(\sqrt n\) spheres: the coordinate envelope and eigenvalue constraint are closed.  Quotienting by the finite sign action therefore leaves a nonempty compact projective space.  On this uniformly positive-definite class, the empirical criteria \(\widehat w\) and \(\widehat g_B(0)\) are continuous in \(B\) and Borel measurable in the finite pilot observations.  Hence their optimizer sets are nonempty and compact for every pilot realization.

For completeness, fix the finite signed pivot-chart list and order it deterministically.  Select the first chart meeting the optimizer set and then minimize its Euclidean coordinates successively over the remaining compact optimizer section.  At each step the coordinate minimum is Borel measurable: for a compact metric section with Borel graph, the event that its minimum is below a rational number is the projection witnessed by a point in a fixed countable dense subset after an arbitrarily small continuous-objective tolerance.  Successive coordinate minimization leaves a singleton, so this construction is precisely the fixed lexicographic chart rule and is measurable.  It proves that the two selectors named by def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator exist and use no data outside the pilot; no fallback outside \(\mathcal K_n\) is introduced.

Define
\[
 M_n=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}
 \lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
 \quad
 d_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal K_n}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|,
 \quad
 e_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal K_n}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|.
 \tag{1}
\]
Lemma lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate gives the pathwise finite-sample inequalities
\[
 d_n\leq C_nM_n,
 \qquad
 e_n\leq2C_nM_n.
 \tag{2}
\]

Since \(w\) and \(g_B(0)\) are continuous on \(\mathcal K_n\), their minimum and maximum are attained.  Choose \(B_n^\star\in\mathcal K_n\) with \(w(B_n^\star)=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}\).  Empirical optimality of \(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}\) gives, for every pilot realization,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 w(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
 &\leq\widehat w(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})+d_n\\
 &\leq\widehat w(B_n^\star)+d_n\\
 &\leq v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+2d_n.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{3}
\]
The reverse inequality \(w(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})\geq v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}\) follows from the definition of the population minimum.  Taking pilot expectations in (3) and using (2) proves
\[
 0\leq
 \mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})-v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}
 \leq2C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
 \tag{4}
\]

Let \(R_n\) be the deterministic envelope constructed in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, so
\[
 0\leq R_n\leq K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}=o(n^{-1}).
 \tag{5}
\]
For \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\), define
\[
 V_s=
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
 \mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
 \operatorname{Var}_\nu
 (\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
 \right].
 \tag{6}
\]
Conditional on the pilot, \(\widehat B_s\) is fixed.  Assumption ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence makes this selected basis independent of both the main assignment and the main potential-outcome array.  The uniform finite ex ante envelope in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence therefore applies at \(B=\widehat B_s\).  Assumption ass:frechet-covariance-domain and thm:fixed-basis-endpoints give
\[
 \sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}\ell_B(c_H)=w(B).
 \tag{7}
\]
The elementary inequality \(|\sup_Hf_H-\sup_Hg_H|\leq\sup_H|f_H-g_H|\), followed by integration over the pilot, now yields
\[
 |V_s-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)|\leq R_n,
 \qquad s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}.
 \tag{8}
\]

The exact sensitivity condition says \(nC_nM_n\to0\) in \(L^1(P)\), hence
\[
 nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{9}
\]
Combining (4) and (9) proves
\[
 \mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
 =v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+o(n^{-1}).
 \tag{10}
\]
Equations (5), (8), and (10) give the displayed feasible Horvitz--Thompson coefficient bridge in the theorem for both selectors.

It remains to quantify the zero-covariance selector.  Choose \(B_n^0\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}\), so \(g_{B_n^0}(0)=g_n^\star\).  Empirical optimality of \(\widehat B_0\) and (1) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 g_n^\star-g_{\widehat B_0}(0)
 &\leq
 |g_{B_n^0}(0)-\widehat g_{B_n^0}(0)|
 +|\widehat g_{\widehat B_0}(0)-g_{\widehat B_0}(0)|\\
 &\leq2e_n.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{11}
\]
Under the displayed deterministic linear error bound in the theorem,
\[
 [q_n-w(\widehat B_0)]_+
 \leq L_n\{g_n^\star-g_{\widehat B_0}(0)\}
 \leq2L_ne_n.
 \tag{12}
\]
Because \(x\geq q-[q-x]_+\), equations (2) and (12) give
\[
 q_n-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
 \leq4L_nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
 \tag{13}
\]
If \(\sup_nL_n<\infty\), equation (9) makes the right side of (13) \(o(n^{-1})\), which is precisely the theorem's zero-surrogate conclusion.  Without the deterministic linear error bound, (11) controls nominal-gain regret but supplies no \(n^{-1}\)-scale control of the worst-loss deficit, so outer argmax consistency alone cannot replace (12).  This completes the proof. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\), the ordinary-inverse loss has the exact intercept--slope form
\[
w(B)=h(0)-a_B+p_\xi(b_B).
\]
Suppose the ordinary-domain zero-covariance and minimax extrema are attained.  Then
\[
\Delta_Z=
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}\{a_B-p_\xi(b_B)\}
-\left[a^\star-\inf_{B:\,a_B=a^\star}p_\xi(b_B)\right].
\]
Consequently strict ordinary-domain improvement holds if and only if \(\Delta_Z>0\), equivalently if and only if there is \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) for which
\[
\inf_{C:\,a_C=a^\star}p_\xi(b_C)-p_\xi(b_B)
>a^\star-a_B.
\]
Thus some slope-penalty advantage must strictly exceed the sacrificed zero-covariance gain.  Through \(q_Z\), all displayed values are unchanged on \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\), and every attained optimizer correspondence there is exactly the inverse image of its projective correspondence.  No universal strictness, minimax interchange, singular completion, or semidefinite reduction is asserted.
statements.justification: This theorem gives the exact ordinary-inverse frontier for when copula-robust residual minimization strictly improves on the zero-covariance optimizer set.
statements.gap: The infimum formulation remains valid on the noncompact positive-definite ordinary domain and isolates precisely the slope-penalty advantage needed to offset sacrificed nominal gain.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The moment-matrix definition gives
\[
Q(c)=Q(0)-cE.
\tag{1}
\]
Using cyclicity of trace in def:gain-loss and the definitions of \(A_B\), \(a_B\), and \(b_B\), equation (1) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
g_B(c)
&=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{A_BQ(0)\}
-cn^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_BE)\\
&=a_B+b_Bc.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
Lemma lem:ht-affine-drift gives \(h(c)=h(0)+2c/n\).  Subtracting (2) from this identity gives
\[
\ell_B(c)=h(0)-a_B+(2/n-b_B)c.
\tag{3}
\]
Taking the maximum of (3) at \(c_L\) and \(c_U\), then invoking the definition of \(p_\xi\), proves
\[
w(B)=h(0)-a_B+p_\xi(b_B).
\tag{4}
\]

Set
\[
M=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}\{a_B-p_\xi(b_B)\}.
\tag{5}
\]
The maximum in (5) exists under the assumed attainment of the ordinary-domain minimax loss, because (4) makes minimizing \(w\) equivalent to maximizing \(a_B-p_\xi(b_B)\).  Equation (4) therefore gives
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)=h(0)-M.
\tag{6}
\]
Attainment of the zero-covariance maximum makes \(a^\star\) and the nonempty equality face
\[
\mathcal A_{0,Z}=\{B\in\mathcal B_Z:a_B=a^\star\}
\]
well defined.  This face need not be compact within the positive-definite ordinary domain, so its penalty is represented by an infimum.  Restricting (4) to the face gives
\[
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_{0,Z}}w(B_0)
=h(0)-a^\star+
\inf_{B:\,a_B=a^\star}p_\xi(b_B).
\tag{7}
\]
Subtracting (6) from (7), and using the definition of \(\Delta_Z\), yields
\[
\Delta_Z
=M-\left[
a^\star-
\inf_{B:\,a_B=a^\star}p_\xi(b_B)
\right].
\tag{8}
\]
This is the asserted exact gap identity.

By (5) and (8), \(\Delta_Z>0\) holds if and only if
\[
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}\{a_B-p_\xi(b_B)\}
>
a^\star-
\inf_{C:\,a_C=a^\star}p_\xi(b_C).
\tag{9}
\]
Because the maximum on the left of (9) is attained, (9) is equivalent to the existence of \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) satisfying
\[
a_B-p_\xi(b_B)
>
a^\star-
\inf_{C:\,a_C=a^\star}p_\xi(b_C).
\]
Rearrangement gives exactly
\[
\inf_{C:\,a_C=a^\star}p_\xi(b_C)-p_\xi(b_B)
>a^\star-a_B.
\tag{10}
\]
Thus strict improvement occurs precisely when some basis's reduction in the endpoint slope penalty strictly exceeds its loss of zero-covariance gain.

Finally, thm:zhao-ordinary-domain-quotient-transfer proves that \(g_B(c)\), \(\ell_B(c)\), and \(w(B)\) are constant on every fiber of the surjection \(q_Z\), and that every attained optimizer correspondence pulls back to its exact inverse image.  Applying that theorem to (4)--(10) proves all assertions on \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\).  No singular class or Moore--Penrose inverse enters the argument. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Assume ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility and the conditions of thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer, including its deterministic linear error bound for the zero-surrogate argmax.  Suppose the attained ordinary-domain optimizer sets satisfy
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}\cup\mathcal A_{0,Z}
\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}.
\]
With \(M_n,C_n,L_n,R_n\) as in that theorem and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, define, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\),
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
Then the finite-\(n\) end-to-end lower bound is
\[
V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}}
\ge
\Delta_Z-(4L_n+2)C_n\mathbb E_PM_n-2R_n.
\]
In particular, if explicit finite constants \(K_M,K_C,K_R\), independent of \(n\), certify
\[
\mathbb E_PM_n\le K_M\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}},
\qquad
C_n\le K_Cn^{\alpha+2\beta-1},
\qquad
R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2},
\]
then the directly checkable condition
\[
\Delta_Z>
(4L_n+2)K_CK_M
\frac{n^{\alpha+2\beta}}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}
+2K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
implies \(V_0>V_{\mathrm{mm}}\) at that finite \(n\).  If, in addition,
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\Delta_Z>0,
\]
then
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n(V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}})>0.
\]
Thus a positive first-order ordinary-domain intercept--slope gap transfers to the feasible independent-pilot estimator, with an explicit finite-\(n\) diagnostic.  The conclusion concerns ex ante expected conditional design variance; it is neither a superpopulation sampling variance nor a Wald limit law.
statements.justification: This proposition converts the ordinary-domain population gap into an end-to-end finite-\(n\) lower bound for two well-defined feasible pilot-selected deployments and supplies a directly checkable strictness condition.
statements.gap: It remains a conditional transfer theorem on the normalized nonempty rate-admissible class and does not turn the fixed triangle witness into an unjustified replicated-network asymptotic family.
statements.consumer: The result is the operational design-side finite-\(n\) diagnostic for independent-pilot deployment.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Assumption ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility ensures that the two pilot-selected bases in def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator are well defined in the nonempty class \(\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\).  For the \(n\)-th problem, put
\[
 v_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B),
 \qquad
 q_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,Z}}w(B).
 \tag{1}
\]
By hypothesis, every attained full ordinary-domain minimax and zero-covariance optimizer lies in \(\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\).  Since \(\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\), a full minimax optimizer is feasible for the restricted problem, and therefore
\[
 v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}=v_n.
 \tag{2}
\]
Likewise, a full zero-covariance optimizer is feasible for the restricted maximization, so the restricted and full maxima agree.  Every restricted maximizer then attains the full maximum and is a full maximizer, while the assumed containment places every full maximizer in the restricted class.  Hence
\[
 \mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\mathcal A_{0,Z}.
 \tag{3}
\]
By def:ordinary-intercept-slope-image and thm:ordinary-inverse-strict-improvement-characterization,
\[
 \Delta_Z=q_n-v_n.
 \tag{4}
\]

Use the notation \(M_n\), \(C_n\), \(L_n\), \(R_n\), and \(V_s\) from the finite inequalities in thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer.  Its robust-selector inequality and its zero-surrogate inequality, together with (2)--(4), imply
\[
 \mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
 \geq
 \Delta_Z-(4L_n+2)C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
 \tag{5}
\]
The two applications of its feasible-estimator bridge give
\[
 V_0\geq\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)-R_n,
 \qquad
 V_{\mathrm{mm}}\leq\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})+R_n.
 \tag{6}
\]
Combining (5) and (6) proves
\[
 \boxed{
 V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}}
 \geq
 \Delta_Z-(4L_n+2)C_n\mathbb E_PM_n-2R_n.}
 \tag{7}
\]
Every term in (7) is either the ordinary-domain population gap, a pilot endpoint sensitivity term, or the explicit feasible-coefficient remainder; no desired variance ordering has been assumed.

We next turn (7) into a directly checkable sufficient condition.  Lemma lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate supplies finite constants \(K_M,K_C<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that for all sufficiently large \(n\), with \(m_{\min}=m_1\wedge m_0\),
\[
 \mathbb E_PM_n\leq K_M\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_{\min}}},
 \qquad
 C_n\leq K_Cn^{\alpha+2\beta-1}.
 \tag{8}
\]
Lemma lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence supplies \(R_n\leq K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}\).  Substitution in (7) gives
\[
V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}}
\ge
\Delta_Z
-(4L_n+2)K_CK_M\frac{n^{\alpha+2\beta}}{\sqrt{m_{\min}}}
-2K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}.
\tag{9}
\]
Therefore the displayed strictness condition in the proposition implies \(V_0>V_{\mathrm{mm}}\) at that finite \(n\).  Any certified constants satisfying (8) and the remainder bound may be used, so this is an audit condition rather than an asymptotic relabeling.

Finally, the exact sensitivity condition in the inherited theorem assumptions gives
\[
 nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{10}
\]
The boundedness of \(L_n\) preserves (10) after multiplication by \(4L_n+2\).  Moreover, \(4\alpha+4\beta<1\) and the remainder bound give
\[
 nR_n\leq K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-1}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{11}
\]
Multiplying (7) by \(n\), taking lower limits, and using (10)--(11) yields
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}n(V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}})
 \geq\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\Delta_Z>0.
\]
The variances in \(V_0\) and \(V_{\mathrm{mm}}\) remain conditional design variances under \(\nu\); the pilot and coupling expectations are only ex ante evaluations.  No statement about the self-normalized variant, a Wald law, or a replicated-triangle sequence is used. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Define \(\iota:\mathcal B_Z\to\mathcal B_Z^+\) by \(\iota([B])=[B]_+\).  This map is a well-defined bijection from \(\mathcal B_Z\) onto
\[
 \{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:\operatorname{rank}(B^{\top}\Omega B)=2\}.
\]
For every \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\) and every \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\),
\[
 g_{\iota(B)}^+(c)=g_B(c),
 \qquad \ell_{\iota(B)}^+(c)=\ell_B(c),
 \qquad w^+(\iota(B))=w(B).
\]

For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), set \(A_e=\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}\) and \(Z_B=\Omega^{1/2}B\).  Every \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\) satisfies
\[
 g_B^+(c_e)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_BA_e),
 \qquad P_B=Z_B(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top},
\]
where \(P_B\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\), \(A_e\succeq0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(P_B)=\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\in\{0,1,2\}\).  On rank two, \([B]_+=\iota([C])\) for a unique \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\), and the gains and losses agree.  If \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\), then for every singular \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\) there is a sequence \([B_j]\in\mathcal B_Z\) such that
\[
 \limsup_{j\to\infty}w(B_j)\le w^+(B).
\]

Suppose ass:exposure-positivity and ass:frechet-covariance-domain hold and \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\).  For the novel Moore--Penrose completion of def:novel-pseudoinverse-completion,
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)
=\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
=\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B).
\]
Define the possibly empty completion equality set
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\}.
\]
Writing \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa)\) for the fixed-threshold argmin, its rank-two stratum is exactly
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\cap\iota(\mathcal B_Z)
=\iota\!\left(
\bigcup_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,
\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing,\ 
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+}}
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa)\right).
\]
In particular, if the ordinary-domain infimum is attained at \(C\in\mathcal B_Z\), then \(\iota(C)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\).  Conversely, if \(\iota(C)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\), then \(C\) attains the ordinary-domain infimum and belongs to \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa_C)\) for some \(\kappa_C>0\) satisfying \(\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_C}}w(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\).  The singular equality stratum is
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\setminus\iota(\mathcal B_Z)
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1,\ w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\}.
\]
A singular equality point need not imply attainment on \(\mathcal B_Z\).  No unconditional completion attainment, no singular equality point, and no attribution of the completion to Zhao is asserted.

For the triangle matrices
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
and the endpoint matrices
\[
Q(c_L)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad A=\frac{I_3+J_3}{4},
\]
the rank-zero and rank-one strata of the novel Moore--Penrose completion obey the exact bounds
\[
\sup_{[B]_+\,:\,\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}g_B^+(0)
=\frac{87}{400}<\frac{31}{80}
\]
and
\[
\inf_{[B]_+\,:\,\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}w^+(B)
=\frac{39}{80}>\frac{2613}{8432}.
\]
More precisely, rank zero has \(g_B^+(0)=0\) and \(w^+(B)=171/200\).  In rank one, after normalizing the unique nonzero arm vector to squared norm three and writing \(u\) for the squared sum of its coordinates, so \(0\le u\le9\), the focal-only stratum has
\[
g_x^+(c_L)=\frac{1195u+6561}{1200(81-4u)},
\qquad g_x^+(c_U)=\frac{243(49-5u)}{400(81-4u)},
\]
whereas the comparison-only stratum has
\[
g_y^+(c_L)=\frac{1240u+729}{150(4u+243)},
\qquad g_y^+(c_U)=\frac{81(48-5u)}{50(4u+243)}.
\]
These rational formulas, together with \(0\le u\le9\), are an exact semialgebraic certificate for both displayed strict inequalities.

There is a positive, fully explicit triangle witness whose strict separation survives every singular stratum of the novel Moore--Penrose completion.  Let \(n=3\), let
\[
G=\begin{bmatrix}0&1&1\\1&0&1\\1&1&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\nu(w)=\left(\frac13\right)^{\sum_iw_i}
       \left(\frac23\right)^{3-\sum_iw_i},
\]
and, writing \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\), define
\[
f_i(w)=
\begin{cases}
1,&w_i=1\text{ and }w_j=w_k=0,\\
0,&w_i=0\text{ and }w_j+w_k\ge1,\\
\star,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Take \(F_1=F_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(\kappa=1/8\).  With \(J_3=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top}\) and \(A=(I_3+J_3)/4\), the exact inputs are
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
\[
c_L=-\frac14,
\qquad c_U=\frac14,
\qquad
Q(c_L)=\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix}.
\]
For normalized rank-two representatives \(B(x,y)\),
\[
\mathcal A_0=\{[B(x,y)]:\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,
\ \mathbf1^{\top}x=\mathbf1^{\top}y=x^{\top}y=0\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\{[B(x,y)]:\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,
\ \mathbf1^{\top}x=x^{\top}y=0,
\ (\mathbf1^{\top}y)^2=216/55\}.
\]
They are nonempty, lie in \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), and satisfy
\[
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\quad w(B_0)=\frac{521}{1200},
\quad w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{2613}{8432},
\quad \lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=\frac4{27}
\]
on the respective equality sets.  Under the rank-two bijection \(\iota:\mathcal B_Z\to\mathcal B_Z^+\), the optimizer sets and values on the full novel completion, including ranks zero and one, are exactly
\[
\mathcal A_0^+=\iota(\mathcal A_0),
\qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\iota(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}),
\]
\[
\max_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\min_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)=\frac{2613}{8432};
\]
in particular, there are no singular optimizer ties.  Consequently \(\xi_0=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\), and
\[
\delta=\frac{4912}{39525},\qquad \eta=\frac5{216}
\]
give the ordinary and completion full-correspondence gaps and the optimizer-wide regularity slack asserted by def:dominance-gap.

For the explicit triangle instance \(\xi_0\) and \(\kappa=1/8\) in thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate, there is a relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) containing \(\xi_0\) such that
\[
\Delta(\xi)>\frac{\delta}{2}=\frac{2456}{39525}
\qquad(\xi\in\mathcal U).
\]
Throughout \(\mathcal U\), the completion optimizer correspondences contain no singular classes and satisfy
\[
\mathcal A_0^+(\xi)=\iota_\xi(\mathcal A_0(\xi)),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+(\xi)=\iota_\xi(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)).
\]
Consequently every ordinary minimax optimizer has lower worst-copula loss than every ordinary zero-covariance optimizer, and every completion minimax optimizer has lower worst-copula loss than every completion zero-covariance optimizer, with each difference exceeding \(\delta/2\).

For the triangle instance of thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate, optimization over the full maximal well-defined unquotiented ordinary-inverse domain \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\) has
\[
\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}g_{q_Z(B)}(0)=q_Z^{-1}(\mathcal A_0),
\qquad
\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}w(q_Z(B))=q_Z^{-1}(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}),
\]
where \(\mathcal A_0\) and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) are exactly the displayed normalized equality sets in that theorem.  Their values are respectively \(31/80\) and \(2613/8432\); every zero-covariance optimizer has worst-copula loss \(521/1200\), so the exact worst-loss reduction is
\[
\frac{521}{1200}-\frac{2613}{8432}=\frac{4912}{39525}>0.
\]
Thus the triangle separation holds on the entire ordinary-inverse matrix domain implicit in Zhao's Equation (8), with optimizer sets enlarged only by independent nonzero column rescaling.  The separate singular-stratum conclusions concern only the note's novel Moore--Penrose completion.

sampling_model.design: A fixed finite network \(G\), known assignment law \(\nu\), known exposure maps \(f_i\), and two mutually exclusive exposure events.
sampling_model.units: The realized finite-population potential outcomes are fixed for design-based estimation; the i.i.d. law \(H\) is used only to choose the basis ex ante.
sampling_model.treatment: The main experiment draws \(W\sim\nu\), and assignment is the only randomness in the causal estimator conditional on the chosen basis.
sampling_model.overlap: Every exposure probability \(\pi_{i,a}\) is positive, and basis covariance is bounded below by \(\kappa\) on the optimization class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Two arm-specific external or historical i.i.d. samples are mutually unpaired and independent of the later assignment; they estimate \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), while the cross-world copula is neither estimated nor assumed.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}\widehat w(B),\quad \widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=(D_{i,1}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}/\pi_{i,1},-D_{i,0}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}/\pi_{i,0})_{i=1}^n,\quad \widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}},\quad \widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)^{\top}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}\)

tldr: Rare network exposures make Horvitz--Thompson estimation noisy, and Zhao's optimal indicator control variates reduce this design variance, but the ex ante basis depends on a cross-world covariance that an unpaired pilot cannot identify. The contribution chain imports the sharp Fréchet covariance range, proves a new fixed-basis affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's objective, poses certified global maximin optimization on the fixed-\(\kappa\) projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency without assuming away ties. Neighborhood persistence is supporting and witness-gated; no strict-dominance region is claimed unless the full-correspondence separation-and-slack certificate is produced.

project_justification.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates explicitly leaves robust basis choice under moment misspecification open; existing Fréchet results identify covariance endpoints, and existing global-optimization results certify Euclidean-box programs, but no paper joins these steps for a block-separable network basis with projective symmetry.
project_justification.niche: Two unpaired pilot marginals identify the exact dependence ambiguity relevant to Zhao's moment matrix while leaving the experimental network and assignment law fixed and known.
project_justification.fill: The project imports the sharp endpoint formulas, proves their affine worst-copula and zero-surrogate frontier inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, formulates a computably specified global maximin certificate on the compact \(\kappa\)-regular projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency. Conditional persistence is supporting: a strict-dominance region requires a separate certified witness with both separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack.

related_work: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates is the direct anchor. MikhaeilGreen2024SharpRegressionAdjustment informs empirical marginal-endpoint consistency through Proposition 1, but neither supplies the independent unpaired product sampling law nor treats interference and an ex ante basis argmax. Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals informs continuity of fixed-marginal coupling correspondences. HarshawMiddletonSavje2026 optimizes conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference; its object is the variance bound rather than the control-variate basis. GaoKleywegt2017DependenceRobust informs the decision-theoretic treatment of dependence ambiguity but studies generic stochastic losses. honest_scope: The sharp Fréchet covariance range is imported from AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, Lemma 1. The new theorem targets are its affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, projective compactness, uniform plug-in value and outer-set consistency, and conditional neighborhood persistence. The finite epsilon-global solver and the separated lawful witness are first-class open constructions. Persistence is incremental and yields a strict-dominance region only after the witness supplies both a positive full-correspondence separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack; no such region is otherwise claimed. No SDP reduction, universal minimax interchange, universal strict improvement, asymptotic normality for the pilot-selected basis, or point convergence under ties is claimed.
